analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Hyperscalers in focus and preview of week; Credit in focus; AI Security; Palantir; TEF/Infra JV; PSON CE) & CFO; JCD
key_insights: Markets are jittery after Meta raised the low end of its 2026 capex guidance, turned free-cash-flow negative and flagged multi-year equity funding needs through new Class C shares. Its CDS spreads widened.

MSFT and GOOGL report Wednesday and AMZN Thursday. These are the key test of the AI spending cycle after Meta's mixed print. Cloud growth rates, sequential trends, backlog conversion, AI versus traditional cloud mix and margins are the focus.
Oracle hosts its Investor Day on Oct 28 (no earnings). Samsung and SK hynix report in Asia.

The Middle East conflict is in its ninth month. Reports point to possible US escalation, and Trump has hinted at renewed strikes on Iran after the Nov 3 midterms. A third carrier strike group is heading toward the Persian Gulf.

Fundamental long/short hedge funds fell 1.1% last week (alpha -0.3%), taking month-to-date losses to 3.8% and giving back a quarter of 2026 gains. On Thursday Oct 22 all three strategies had drawdowns above 1% on the same day, the first time since COVID.
GS Research cut its KOSPI target to 9,000 after a 40% index decline but still sees attractive risk/reward. Forward P/E is 4x, three standard deviations below the mean.
Moody's held France at Aa3 with a negative outlook. S&P and Fitch both downgraded France in 2025. The desk's preference is Orange.

GS chief credit strategist Amanda Lynam: off-balance-sheet leases and purchase commitments across five leading hyperscalers total $2.8 trillion, up eightfold since 2023. S&P adjusts leverage for off-balance-sheet leases while Moody's and Fitch do not, so methodology changes are worth watching.
Elon Musk said SpaceX closed $40 billion in debt financing.

Lee Coppersmith sees the sell-off as a positioning and leverage unwind rather than an AI fundamentals collapse. TMT-focused funds are down nearly 10% month-to-date with about $20bn of TMT selling in two weeks. Gross leverage remains elevated. Risk is that discretionary selling turns into systematic CTA selling. His base case is a relief rally, held cautiously, and he prefers call spreads to outright longs.
Nikesh Arora (All-In podcast) says AI-accelerated cyber threats create a new category needing security. Agents raise accountability issues, and controls lag AI deployment.
Amazon CEO Jassy says AWS 2026 cloud capacity is sold out, most large 2027 capacity blocks are booked, and a meaningful share of 2028 is committed.

Ramp reports two consecutive months of virtually no growth in token spending while token volumes rose, as falling effective prices and efficient models absorb usage. Gavin Baker argues revenue per GPU relative to rental cost is the relevant measure, and falling token prices do not imply weaker GPU demand.
MSFT is up 38% since the July print. GIR sees Azure cc growth of 46-47% vs Street 45% (guide 44-45%). Debate is on AI unit economics/ROIC and FY28 capex (GSe $319bn vs Street $252bn).

GOOGL: debate is Search resilience vs agentic AI disruption (GIR -1% vs consensus on Q3 Search). GIR expects Cloud revenue growth near +100% y/y vs consensus +96% and Q2 +82%. GIR capex is $350bn for 2027.
AMZN: consensus AWS growth about 41% and margin 37% (prior quarter +37% y/y, ~39% margin). Capex is around $220bn for 2026. Reported idle NVDA racks due to power shortages are a focus.

ORCL Investor Day questions: execution on the 10GW capacity roadmap given power bottlenecks, capex intensity and timing (peak said to be 27-28), demand sustainability and customer concentration, and upside to FY26-30 targets.

Palantir: after GIR's Oct 8 upgrade to Buy, investor positioning is balanced. GIR sees scope for significant upward estimate revisions even as growth slows. The 60x multiple implies about 1.3x P/E/G vs 2.0x for large-cap software peers.
Infosys 2QFY27 was largely in line with a second consecutive guidance cut (mid-point implies modest negative FY27 organic growth), sluggish demand and range-bound margins.
SK hynix is reportedly considering a special dividend of about W16tn (about 80% of an estimated W20tn Kioxia stake sale profit), with an announcement slated for Oct 28.
Optimum Communications (formerly Altice USA) is reportedly preparing a Chapter 11 filing before end of 2026 to restructure about $26 billion of debt, with senior lenders taking majority ownership.
Telefonica and Indra are in preliminary talks on a European sovereign cloud JV. Away from GS, JPMorgan cut Telefonica to Underweight with a EUR 3.20 PT.
US trading floor saw about $20bn net TMT selling over two weeks, approaching the -$23bn during the July AI selling episode. There were no signs of offense on AI.
Week ahead: S&P implied move through Oct 30 is 1.80%. FOMC and BOC Wednesday, ECB Thursday, BOJ Friday. 44% of S&P market cap reports earnings.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang sees low likelihood of memory oversupply through 2029. Samsung is in the final phase of equipment investment at Taylor Fab 1, targeting 2nm capacity of 20k wafers per month by 2H27.

Meta faces publisher opposition to commercial terms effective Oct 30 that could allow scraping of business-account sites without opt-out. The News/Media Alliance asked for withdrawal by Oct 26, and EU and UK competition complaints have been filed.

European tech and telco previews: STM bar is above 3.75bn Q3 revenue, Orange consensus EBITDA growth 4.1% vs GIR 4.8%, TMUS expected in line with EBITDA $9.41bn, Adyen GIR 2H26 organic ex-fx growth 20.8%.

Orange preferred. Consolidation and French politics drive the shares.

earnings_insights: MSFT Q1 FY27 preview (reports Wed): GIR expects Azure cc growth of 46-47% vs Street 45% cc and a guide of 46-47% for Q2 FY27. FY28 capex GSe $319bn vs Street $252bn.
GOOGL Q3 preview (reports Wed): GIR expects Search about 1% below consensus and Cloud revenue growth near +100% y/y vs consensus +96% (Q2 actual +82%). GIR 2027 capex is $350bn.
AMZN Q3 preview (reports Thu): consensus AWS revenue growth about 41% and margin 37% vs prior quarter actual +37% y/y and ~39% margin. 2026 capex around $220bn.
Meta (already reported): raised low end of 2026 capex guidance, turned free-cash-flow negative and flagged equity funding via Class C shares.

TMUS Q3 preview: GIR EBITDA $9.41bn (consensus $9.41bn, guidance just above $9.4bn), revenue $23.12bn vs consensus $23.18bn, service revenue $19.33bn vs consensus $19.31bn. Shareholder returns authorised up to $18.2bn in 2026.
Orange Q3 preview: consensus EBITDA growth 4.1% vs GIR 4.8%.
Adyen Q3 preview: forecast 21.5% y/y ex-fx (19.5% organic) for 3Q and 23.7% ex-fx (21.9% organic) for 4Q. GIR expects 2H26 organic ex-fx growth of 20.8%.
DSY: Q3 and FY26 guidance 3-5%, with GIR and consensus near 4%. GIR 2027 guidance estimate 5% vs consensus near 6%. CMD Nov 17.
Capgemini: raised organic growth forecast to 3.8% for Q3 and 3.2% for Q4, implying 4.1% for FY26. FY27 consensus is 3.2%.
Tieto: GIR cut FY26 organic revenue growth to about -5% y/y vs guidance of -3% to -5% and Street -3.7%.
Indra: FY26 guidance of more than EUR 7bn constant-currency revenue and more than EUR 700m reported EBIT vs Visible Alpha consensus EUR 6.95bn and EUR 705m. Defence backlog EUR 11.7bn at June.
STM: bar is above 3.75bn Q3 revenue. Gross margin 2027 Visible Alpha 39.9% vs GIR 39.3%.
Infosys 2QFY27 (reported): second consecutive guidance cut, strong deal wins on one mega deal, margins range-bound.
Samsung preliminary results were slightly ahead on revenues. SK hynix reports Oct 28.
Palantir: GIR upside case about $6.50 in 2029 GAAP EPS, stock at 0.50x PEG on that case.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud growth is accelerating (GIR sees Azure 46-47% cc and Google Cloud about +100%), AWS capacity is sold out through 2026 and largely booked for 2027, so spending is backed by demand.
tension_points.bear_case: Meta turned FCF negative and needs equity funding, off-balance-sheet commitments total $2.8 trillion, and markets want growth without another spending shock.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further equity issuance or balance-sheet pressure at MSFT, GOOGL or AMZN, or a capex raise not matched by cloud growth.

tension_points.bull_case: Hedge fund unwind and defensive positioning set up a relief rally if MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN and the Fed restore confidence.
tension_points.bear_case: Gross leverage is elevated and discretionary selling can turn into systematic CTA selling, with vol signalling stress.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A transition from discretionary selling into systematic CTA supply if markets weaken further.
